reviewer.role: independent bounded discovery storage probe reviewer

verdict: The stabilized storage source passes all three requested /private/tmp adversarial probe groups. R1 storage blockers for retained checkout validation, cleanup lock lifetime and foreign-byte boundary are closed in this source. Pending-plan reservation reconstruction/binding remains an explicitly deferred graph integration gate and is not raised as a new storage defect in this review.
scope: Read-only review of the stabilized discovery_storage.py source with isolated temporary checkout/process probes only. No source, schema, test, Git, network, connector, real Vault, or human gate was mutated.

closed_r1_findings.note: Pending-plan reservation remains intentionally awaiting the validated graph binding on open and each prospective install; this R2 storage-only review does not reclassify it.

closed_r1_findings.evidence: open_store parses retained pyproject bytes with tomllib.loads after descriptor-relative tree.file; no resolve_checkout_root pathname validator remains (lines 403-425).
open_store duplicates checkout_fd for the flock and closes tree descriptors before closing the duplicate lock descriptor (lines 405-410, 444-454); the cleanup-window probe kept the contender busy.
The exception boundary maps STAGING_CONFLICT to DISCOVERY_CONFLICT (lines 439-442), while final retained-tree verification still has WORK_PATH_UNSAFE precedence for a foreign set change.

probes.kind: two-process lock contention with delayed descriptor cleanup
probes.method: Process A entered open_store, then its patched first close_fd call wrote cleanup-started and slept 2 seconds. Process B attempted open_store while A was in tree.close; no .work/research was present.

After retained descriptor-relative pyproject capture, the checkout directory was renamed and replaced; the replacement pyproject.toml was a symlink to an outside temporary file. os.open was instrumented to count pathname opens of the replacement path.

probes.kind: foreign exact-byte appearance after retained missing target
probes.method: Patched the atomic installer to create the target with foreign bytes equal to the requested bytes before invoking the real installer.

probes.kind: foreign differing-byte appearance after retained missing target
probes.method: Patched the atomic installer to create the target with differing foreign bytes before invoking the real installer.

probe_interpretation: The cleanup probe establishes that the duplicate flock descriptor remains live through tree.close; no lock file or lease artifact is written.
The checkout swap probe exercises the retained named checkout edge and confirms the replacement path is never opened by the validator.

Both foreign-target races are refused by final retained named-edge/set verification. Same-byte appearance is not treated as idempotent reuse; differing-byte internal staging conflict is normalized but final WORK_PATH_UNSAFE correctly wins.
remaining_gates: Bind a validated graph-derived pending plan on open and before every prospective install, then re-run capacity/recovery vectors; this is the parent-declared integration gate.
Run full local Python suites, installed-wheel/resource parity and fresh four-job CI against the exact integrated head; Linux flock behavior remains a delivery gate.
Provider capability, real-data, Vault/admin and human scientific gates remain outside this storage probe review.
